pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Paying in a US restaurant has its own habits. Look at the cards and guess.

cards.note: Servers don’t usually bring it until you ask, so it feels polite and not rushed.
A tip is usually 15–20% of the bill for good service, and it is not included.
You can ask for “separate checks” and each person pays only their own.

qs.q: How do you ask for the bill?

levels.A2: Could we have the check, please?
levels.B1: Excuse me, could we have the check when you get a chance?
levels.B2: Whenever you have a moment, could we get the check, please?

qs.pt: Quanto as pessoas dão de gorjeta?

levels.A2: Fifteen to twenty percent of the bill.
levels.B1: Most people leave 15–20% for good service.
levels.B2: Between 15 and 20 percent is the norm in a sit-down restaurant, and many leave more for great service.

qs.q: What can you say to split the bill?

levels.B1: Could we split it? Each person pays their own.
levels.B2: Could we split the check evenly, or would you mind separating it?

pages.compare: In Brazil the service charge of 10% is often on the bill, and you can say “pode trazer a conta?”. In the USA the tip is added by you. How do you pay where you live?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.focus: Weak words: the, a, to, of
pages.tip: Small words are weak: “the” sounds like “thuh”, “a” like “uh”, “of” like “uhv”. Keep them short and quiet.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Could we have the check, please? Separate checks.
ladder.goal: Ask and choose how to pay.

ladder.say: I think there is a mistake on the bill. We didn’t order this.
Would you mind splitting this so each of us pays for our own meal?
I’d be happy to cover the tip, if everyone else can take care of the rest.
ladder.goal: Negotiate how to share a cost.

ladder.say: Allow me to settle this one; you can get the next, if you’d like.
ladder.goal: Handle the social side of paying.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
